records.quote: Theorem 4.1 Let X_{lambda_1}, X_lambda be independent nonnegative random variables with X_{lambda_1} ~ F(lambda_1 t) and X_lambda ~ F(lambda t), where lambda_1, lambda > 0 and F is an absolutely continuous distribution. Let Y_{lambda*_1}, Y_lambda be independent nonnegative random variables with Y_{lambda*_1} ~ F(lambda*_1 t) and Y_lambda ~ F(lambda t), where lambda*_1, lambda > 0. Let r be the reverse hazard rate function of F. Assume tr(t) and tr'(t)/r(t) are both decreasing in t. Suppose lambda*_1 = min(lambda, lambda_1, lambda*_1), then (lambda_1, lambda) <=^w (lambda*_1, lambda) => r*_{2:2}(t)/r_{2:2}(t) is increasing in t.
records.family: scale model F(lambda_i t): system A = {X_{lambda_1}, X_lambda}, system B = {Y_{lambda*_1}, Y_lambda}

records.quote: Theorem 4.5 Let X_1, ..., X_n be independent nonnegative random variables such that X_i ~ F(lambda_1 t) for i = 1, ..., p and X_j ~ F(lambda t) for j = p+1, ..., n, with lambda_1, lambda > 0 and F is an absolutely continuous distribution. Let Y_1, ..., Y_n be independent nonnegative random variables with Y_i ~ F(lambda*_1 t) for i = 1, ..., p and Y_j ~ F(lambda t) for j = p+1, ..., n, with lambda*_1, lambda > 0. Let r be the reverse hazard rate function of F. Assume tr(t) and tr'(t)/r(t) are both decreasing in t. Suppose lambda*_1 = min(lambda, lambda_1, lambda*_1), then (lambda_1,...,lambda_1, lambda,...,lambda; p of lambda_1, q of lambda) <=^w (lambda*_1,...,lambda*_1, lambda,...,lambda; p of lambda*_1, q of lambda) => r*_{n:n}(t)/r_{n:n}(t) is increasing in t, where q = n - p.
